title: Section 332 — House-trespass in order to commit offence

content.overview: BNS s. 332 — House-trespass in order to commit offence.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
House-trespass in order to commit offence. BNS restatement of IPC 451. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 451. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 332 is the rule on “House-trespass in order to commit offence”. The section provides that whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 332 exists so that “House-trespass in order to commit offence” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

The provision in detail
332. Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence–

(a) punishable with death, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;

(b) punishable with imprisonment for life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;

(c) punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine:

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence–
2. (a) punishable with death, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;
3. (b) punishable with imprisonment for life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;
4. (c) punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine:

Exceptions, limitations and provisos
Provided that if the offence intended to be committed is theft, the term of the imprisonment may be extended to seven years

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 332 (House-trespass in order to commit offence), Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence–
   (2) (a) punishable with death, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;
   (3) (b) punishable with imprisonment for life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;
   (4) (c) punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine:
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 332 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 332 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 332 constitutes a key component of Chapter XVII (Of Offences against Property) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing house-trespass in order to commit offence. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of house-trespass in order to commit offence under Section 332 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 332.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 332 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 332 vs General Attempt: Section 332 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XVII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.
Section 332 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 332 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences against Property.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 332 for conduct relating to house-trespass in order to commit offence.
Rule: Under BNS s. 332, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 332.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 332 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
